alternatives_rejected.config_field: A per-run, temporary evaluation knob is not a lasting user preference.
alternatives_rejected.delete_now_revert_later: Loses per-run choice; the revert would conflict with later edits to the same lines.
alternatives_rejected.sase_feature_flag: Flags are sase-project only; wrong scope for a plugin macro.

caveats: You may not need the change to start evaluating. Plain `#research_swarm` (no linker), `#research`, and `#research/more` already publish real tables, so `bob ref create` table rendering can be judged on existing reports today.

The real lever is the renderer. Per pandoc's pipe-table rule, when any row exceeds `--columns` (72), column widths come from the separator dash counts, so `|---|---|` gives equal-width wrapped columns. A renderer-side fix (a Lua filter that sizes columns from content, or proportional separator dashes) would help every producer, not just linker runs.
Interface creep: this is the 24th input on an already large macro, and temporary inputs tend to stick. Decide by a date whether to delete it.
Only linker runs (`linker`/`image`/`diagrams`/`audio`) are affected; the plan deliberately does not make the flag imply the linker.
plan_assessment.suggested_follow_up: After a few real PDFs with tables, either delete the input and its true arms, or keep tables and fix widths in the renderer instead.
plan_assessment.summary: A default-off per-run macro input is the right reversible step: it gives the end state you want today, keeps the carefully tuned conversion rule tested instead of rotting in git history, and removal later is a mechanical delete of the true arms.
why_right: Easier to re-enable than `git revert c787c88`; that revert would now conflict with later diagram-era edits that reference the rule ("converted from a table into a list", the `:::` sentence, "or a diagram").
Per-run granularity fits an evaluation: you can A/B the same topic with and without conversion.
Matches the existing linker-modifier pattern (`linker_model`, `audio_edition`): it never adds an agent, so no execution-matrix churn.
A SASE feature flag does not fit: flags are a sase-project concern, and this lives in a plugin as a per-run choice.
